about: Staffordshire and other English potters' marks, read from Godden (1964) by Heirloom (hallmark-sources/staffordshire, build_marks.py). Each drawn mark is cut from the book and credited; marks Godden sets in type are words only.

godden-encyclopaedia-1964.author: Geoffrey A. Godden
godden-encyclopaedia-1964.title: Encyclopaedia of British Pottery and Porcelain Marks
godden-encyclopaedia-1964.note: Pages checked in Joe's copy, 2026-11-24. Doulton & Co., Burslem p. 213; Lambeth pp. 214-219 (artists' monograms pp. 216-218, Doulton & Watts p. 219).

entries.name: Johnson Bros. (Hanley) Ltd.
entries.works: Hanley Pottery (and other Hanley Potteries), Hanley (and at Tunstall, c. 1899–1913)
entries.notes: Formerly J. W. Pankhurst & Co.

entries.name: Alfred Meakin (Ltd.)
entries.works: Royal Albert, Victoria and Highgate Potteries, Tunstall
entries.notes: Firm retitled "Alfred Meakin (Tunstall) Ltd." from c. 1913. Newfield Pottery taken over c. 1930.

entries.name: Alfred Meakin (Tunstall) Ltd.
entries.works: Royal Albert, Victoria and Highgate Potteries, Tunstall (Newfield Pottery taken over c. 1930)
entries.notes: Title of Alfred Meakin (Ltd.) from c. 1913; Godden prints this as a sub-heading above 2590–5.

entries.name: Charles Meakin
entries.notes: Formerly at Burslem.

entries.name: J. & G. Meakin (Ltd.)
entries.works: Eagle Pottery and Eastwood Works, Hanley
entries.notes: Eastwood Pottery sold 1958; Eagle Pottery then enlarged and modernised.

entries.name: W. H. Grindley & Co. (Ltd.)
entries.works: New Field Pottery (c. 1880–91), Woodland Pottery (1891– ), Tunstall
entries.notes: Firm acquired by Alfred Clough Ltd. in 1960. "Ltd." added to style and marks from 1925.

entries.name: Grindley Hotel Ware Co. Ltd.
entries.notes: A separate company; its marks are shown with the W. H. Grindley entry on the previous page.

entries.name: Myott, Son & Co. (Ltd.)
entries.works: Alexander Pottery, Stoke (1898–1902), Cobridge (1902–46) and Hanley (c. 1947– )
entries.notes: Formerly G. T. Mountford, q.v.

entries.name: Thomas Booth & Co.
entries.works: Knowles Works, Burslem (c. 1868) and Church (Bank) Works, Tunstall
entries.notes: Subsequently Thomas Booth & Son, q.v.

entries.name: Thomas Booth & Son
entries.notes: Formerly T. Booth & Co., q.v. Subsequently T. G. Booth, q.v.

entries.name: Thomas G. Booth
entries.notes: Formerly T. Booth & Son, q.v. Subsequently T. G. & F. Booth, q.v.

entries.name: T. G. & F. Booth
entries.notes: Formerly T. G. Booth, q.v. Subsequently Booths (Ltd.), see next entry.

entries.name: Booths (Limited)
entries.works: Church Bank Pottery (and Swan and Soho Potteries from c. 1912), Tunstall
entries.notes: Formerly T. G. & F. Booth. Subsequently Booths & Colcloughs Ltd., see next entry.

entries.name: Booths & Colcloughs Ltd.
entries.notes: Formerly Booths Ltd. and Colclough China Ltd., q.v. Continued as Ridgway, Adderley, Booths & Colcloughs Ltd. from January 1st 1955 and retitled Ridgway Potteries Ltd. from February 28th, 1955. See page 536.

entries.name: Jacob & Thomas Furnival
entries.notes: Subsequently Thomas Furnival & Co., q.v.

entries.name: Thomas Furnival & Co.
entries.notes: Formerly Jacob & Thomas Furnival, q.v. Subsequently Furnival & Clark.

entries.name: Thomas Furnival & Sons
entries.notes: Subsequently Furnivals, see next entry.

entries.name: Furnivals (Ltd.)
entries.notes: Formerly Thomas Furnival & Sons. Style changed to "FURNIVALS (1913) LTD" in January 1913. "LTD" added to style c. 1895.

entries.name: John Maddock
entries.notes: Formerly Maddock & Seddon, q.v. Subsequently J. Maddock & Son(s), see next entry.

entries.name: John Maddock & Sons (Ltd.)
entries.works: Newcastle St. and Dale Hall, Burslem
entries.notes: Formerly J. Maddock, see previous entry. "& Son" added to style in 1855; "Ltd." added to marks after 1896.

entries.name: Wood & Son(s) (Ltd.)
entries.works: Trent and New Wharf Potteries, Burslem
entries.notes: Early wares unmarked. Trading as Wood & Sons (Holdings) Ltd. from 1954. 'Wood & Son' changed to 'Wood & Sons' from c. 1907; 'Ltd.' from c. 1910.

entries.name: Charles James Mason
entries.works: Fenton Works, Lane Delph (also, 1851-4, Daisy Bank, Longton)
entries.notes: Formerly Charles James Mason & Co., see next entry.

entries.name: Charles James Mason & Co.
entries.works: Patent Ironstone China Manufactory (Fenton Stone Works), Lane Delph
entries.notes: Formerly G. M. and C. J. Mason, q.v. Subsequently C. J. Mason, q.v. Several printed marks occur with initials C. J. M. & Co. or title C. J. Mason & Co., 1829-45.

entries.name: G. M. & C. J. Mason
entries.works: Patent Ironstone China Manufactory, Lane Delph
entries.notes: Also listed in rates, etc., as G. & C. Mason. Subsequently C. J. Mason & Co., q.v.

entries.name: Miles Mason
entries.works: Islington Pottery, Liverpool (c. 1792–1800); Victoria Pottery (c. 1800–6); Minerva Works, Lane Delph (c. 1806–16)

entries.name: G. L. Ashworth & Bros. (Ltd.)
entries.notes: Succeeded Francis Morley, q.v. Used Mason's Patent Ironstone marks (Godden: first adopted the printed mark originally used by Masons; own name added; 'England' added 1891).

entries.name: Josiah Spode
entries.notes: Subsequently Copeland & Garrett, q.v.

entries.name: W. T. Copeland (& Sons Ltd.)
entries.notes: Formerly Copeland & Garrett, q.v.

entries.name: Copeland & Garrett
entries.notes: Formerly Spode, q.v. Subsequently W. T. Copeland.

entries.name: Josiah Wedgwood (& Sons Ltd.)
entries.wares: Earthenwares, Basaltes, Jaspers, Porcelains, Parian, Majolica, etc.
entries.notes: Formerly in partnership with Thomas Whieldon. Very early wares unmarked; experimental examples with an incised signature or the initials J. W. Godden's WARNING: several other potters used the name Wedgwood (or close imitations); English copyists listed on page 655. No true Wedgwood marks include "& Co." or a middle "E". Many of the standard marks occur with slight additions (artist, designer, body, pattern). Includes Godden's table of impressed year letters (pages 658-659).

entries.name: Wedgwood & Bentley partnership
entries.notes: Partnership of Josiah Wedgwood and Thomas Bentley. Marks used only on ornamental wares.

entries.name: Wedgwood & Co. (Ltd.)
entries.works: Unicorn and Pinnox Works, Tunstall (Staffordshire Potteries)
entries.notes: Formerly Podmore, Walker & Co., q.v. N.B. The marks of this firm are often mistaken for those of Josiah Wedgwood & Sons Ltd. The Tunstall firm includes "& Co." in the style and marks. This "Wedgwood & Co." mark was also used at the Ferrybridge Pottery, see page 246. "Ltd." added to style and marks from 1900.

entries.name: Ralph Wedgwood (& Co.)
entries.works: Burslem, c. 1785-96; Ferrybridge Pottery, Yorkshire, c. 1796-1801 (see page 246)
entries.notes: Dates approximate only.

entries.name: Minton (various titles)
entries.notes: Early wares generally unmarked or bear the pattern number only. Later titles Mintons Ltd.

entries.name: Ridgway & Abington
entries.notes: Formerly W. Ridgway, Son & Co., q.v. Partners Edward James Ridgway and Leonard James Abington; Abington occurs with one and with two b's. Subsequently E. J. Ridgway.

entries.name: Job Ridgway
entries.notes: Formerly Job & George Ridgway. Subsequently Job Ridgway & Sons.

entries.name: Job Ridgway & Sons
entries.notes: Formerly Job Ridgway. Subsequently J. & W. Ridgway.

entries.name: John Ridgway (& Co.)
entries.notes: Formerly J. & W. Ridgway. Subsequently Ridgway, Bates & Co.

entries.name: John & William Ridgway
entries.works: Cauldon Place and Bell Works, Shelton, Hanley (Staffordshire Potteries)
entries.notes: Formerly Job Ridgway & Sons.

entries.name: John Ridgway Bates & Co.
entries.notes: Subsequently Bates, Brown-Westhead-Moore & Co., q.v.

entries.name: Ridgway, Morley, Wear & Co.
entries.notes: Formerly Hicks, Meigh & Johnson. Subsequently Ridgway & Morley.

entries.name: Ridgway & Morley
entries.notes: Formerly Ridgway, Morley Wear & Co.

entries.name: Ridgway Potteries Ltd.
entries.works: Ash Hall, Stoke (Staffordshire Potteries); group potteries: Booths (Church Bank Pottery, Tunstall), Colcloughs (Regent Works, Longton), Paladin Works (Fenton), North Staffordshire Pottery (Cobridge), Portland Pottery (Cobridge), Bedford Works (Shelton), Adderley Floral China Works (Longton), Gainsborough Works (Longton)
entries.notes: Formerly Ridgway & Adderley Ltd., see page 539. Ash Hall is the administrative address. Many marks include the name of the pottery concerned.

entries.name: Ridgway & Robey
entries.notes: Partners William Ridgway and Ralph Mayer Robey.

entries.name: Ridgway, Sparks & Ridgway
entries.notes: Formerly E. J. Ridgway & Son. Subsequently Ridgways.

entries.name: William Ridgway (& Co.)
entries.works: Bell Works, Shelton, and Church Works, Hanley (Staffordshire Potteries)
entries.notes: Formerly J. & W. Ridgway, q.v. William Ridgway Son & Co. were also working at Hanley c. 1838-48. Some W. Ridgway marks were later reissued by Ridgways, see page 539.

entries.name: William Ridgway, Son & Co.
entries.works: Church Works (and Cobden Works c. 1841-6), Hanley (Staffordshire Potteries)
entries.notes: Subsequently Ridgway & Abington.

entries.name: Ridgways
entries.notes: Formerly Ridgway Sparks & Ridgway, q.v. Continued as Ridgways (Bedford Works) Ltd. Retitled Ridgway & Adderley Ltd. October 21st 1952 (old marks continued); with Booths & Colcloughs Ltd. from January 1st 1955 as Ridgway, Adderley, Booths & Colcloughs Ltd.; renamed Ridgway Potteries Ltd. from February 28th 1955.

entries.name: Ridgways (Bedford Works) Ltd.
entries.notes: Formerly Ridgways. Former marks of Ridgways continued. Retitled Ridgway & Adderley Ltd. from October 21st 1952; became Ridgway Potteries Ltd. from February 28th 1955, see page 536.

entries.name: Adams & Bromley
entries.wares: Earthenwares, Jasper wares, Parian, Majolica, etc.
entries.notes: Formerly John Adams & Co.

entries.name: Adams & Cooper
entries.notes: Subsequently Edward Adams.

entries.name: Harvey Adams & Co.
entries.works: High Street and Sutherland Road, Longton
entries.notes: Formerly Adams & Scrivener. Subsequently Hammersley & Co.

entries.name: John Adams & Co.
entries.wares: Earthenwares, Jasper wares, Parian, Majolica, etc.
entries.notes: Subsequently Adams & Bromley, q.v.

entries.name: William Adams & Sons (Potters) Ltd.
entries.works: Greengates etc., Tunstall and Stoke (earlier titles: W. Adams, W. Adams & Co., W. Adams & Son)
entries.notes: Earlier titles W. Adams, W. Adams & Co., W. Adams & Son.

entries.name: Davenport
entries.notes: Various styles: W. Davenport & Co., Davenports Ltd., etc. See Jewitt's Ceramic Art of Great Britain (1878 and 1883).

entries.name: Davenport Banks & Co.
entries.notes: Subsequently Davenport Beck & Co.

entries.name: Davenport Beck & Co.
entries.notes: Formerly Davenport Banks & Co.

entries.name: Enoch Wood
entries.notes: Continued as Wood & Caldwell. Enoch Wood died in 1840.

entries.name: Wood & Caldwell
entries.notes: Continued from Enoch Wood; continued as Enoch Wood & Sons. Pointer also at 4256 on p695 'WOOD & CALDWELL / See Enoch Wood'.

entries.name: Enoch Wood & Sons
entries.notes: Continued from Wood & Caldwell. Exported vast amounts of pottery to North America (one shipment to a Philadelphia china broker totalled 262,000 pieces).

entries.name: James & Ralph Clews
entries.notes: Works rented from William Adams in September 1817; the firm became bankrupt in 1834 or 1835. Described on bill-heads as 'Potters to Her Imperial Majesty, the Empress of all the Russians'.

entries.name: Andrew Stevenson
entries.notes: Formerly Bucknall & Stevenson.

entries.name: Ralph Stevenson
entries.notes: Many Stevenson marks may have been used by either Andrew or Ralph Stevenson. See Antiques magazine, June 1955 (N. Emery) for the Stevenson family.

entries.name: Ralph Stevenson & Son
entries.notes: From c. 1832 to 1835; follows Ralph Stevenson.

entries.name: Stevenson & Hancock (and subsequent owners)
entries.notes: Formerly Stevenson, Sharpe & Co. See also under Derby Porcelain Works. Not a Staffordshire firm. Subsequent owners of the King Street works continued the S. H. mark until the concern was bought by the Royal Crown Derby Company in 1935.

entries.name: Stevenson, Sharp & Co.
entries.notes: Formerly Locker & Co. Subsequently Stevenson & Hancock. Not a Staffordshire firm.

entries.name: Stevenson, Spencer & Co. Ltd.
entries.notes: Distributors only from 1960.

entries.name: Stevenson & Williams
entries.notes: A short-lived partnership between Ralph Stevenson and Aldborough Lloyd Williams; not listed in directories but mentioned in a mortgage deed of 1825.

entries.name: Elijah Mayer
entries.notes: Subsequently E. Mayer & Son.

entries.name: Elijah Mayer & Son
entries.notes: Formerly E. Mayer. In most rate records the name of Joseph Mayer is given, but directories give the trading name E. Mayer & Son.

entries.name: Mayer & Elliott
entries.works: Fountain Place and Dale Hall, Longport
entries.notes: Formerly Mayer Bros. & Elliott. Subsequently Liddle Elliott & Son. Godden's heading spells it ELLIOTT; his note elsewhere gives Elliot.

entries.name: Joseph Mayer & Co.
entries.works: High St., Church Works from 1831, Hanley
entries.notes: Joseph Mayer was the son of Elijah and continued his father's works probably under various styles (E. Mayer & Co., J. Mayer & Co., or Mayer & Co.). The exact period is open to question.

entries.name: Thomas Mayer
entries.works: Cliff Bank Works, Stoke (c. 1826–35), and Brook St., Longport (c. 1836–8)
entries.notes: Blue printed wares were extensively exported to the United States and American devices occur in the marks.

entries.name: Thomas, John & Joseph Mayer (T. J. & J. Mayer; Mayer Bros.)
entries.works: Furlong Works and Dale Hall Pottery, Burslem
entries.notes: Exhibited in 1851, 1853 and 1855; moulded parian wares a feature. Subsequently Mayer Bros. & Elliot.

entries.name: Mayer & Maudesley
entries.notes: Ward's Stoke-on-Trent (1843) lists the firm as producing 'China toys, also Black Egyptian' (basaltes).

entries.name: Mayer & Newbold
entries.works: "Staffordshire Porcelain Manufactory", Market Place, Lane End
entries.notes: Formerly T. & J. Johnson. Subsequently Richard Newbold.

entries.name: Thomas C. Wild & Co.
entries.notes: Continued as Thomas C. Wild.

entries.name: Thomas C. Wild
entries.notes: Continued as Thomas C. Wild & Sons (Ltd.).

entries.name: Thomas C. Wild & Sons (Ltd.)
entries.notes: Makers of Royal Albert china.

entries.name: John Aynsley & Sons (Ltd.)
entries.notes: The early wares were unmarked.

entries.name: Wileman & Co.
entries.works: Foley Potteries and Foley China Works, Fenton, Longton
entries.notes: Subsequently Shelley's, see Shelley Potteries Ltd. Continued James F. Wileman.

entries.name: Shelley Potteries Ltd.
entries.notes: Formerly Wileman & Co., q.v. N.B. Name Shelley formerly used by Wileman & Co.

entries.name: Star China Co.
entries.notes: Subsequently Paragon China (Co.) Ltd.

entries.name: Paragon China (Co.) Ltd.
entries.notes: Formerly Star China Company, q.v. Taken over by T. C. Wild & Sons Ltd. in 1960 but continued under the same title. Trade-name Paragon used on marks by Star China Co. from c. 1900.

entries.name: Derby Crown Porcelain Company Ltd.
entries.notes: Listed under DERBY (Derby Porcelain Works entry, 'Royal Crown Porcelain Co.'); predecessor of Royal Crown Derby Porcelain Co. Ltd.

entries.name: Royal Crown Derby Porcelain Co. Ltd.
entries.notes: Takes over the King Street factory in 1935 (see Stevenson & Hancock).

entries.name: Coalport Porcelain Works (John Rose & Co.)
entries.notes: The early Coalport porcelains are mostly unmarked.

entries.name: Burgess & Leigh (Ltd.)
entries.works: Hill Pottery, c. 1867–89, Middleport Pottery, c. 1889+, Burslem
entries.notes: Staffordshire Potteries. Makers of Burleigh ware. Mark entries 720–5 are cross-referenced from BURLEIGH.

firms.title: A. J. Wilkinson and Clarice Cliff

entries.name: Arthur J. Wilkinson (Ltd.)
entries.works: Royal Staffordshire Pottery (and formerly at Central Pottery), Burslem
entries.notes: Staffordshire Potteries. Formerly Wilkinson & Hulme.

entries.name: Newport Pottery Co. Ltd.
entries.notes: Staffordshire Potteries.

entries.name: Grimwade Bros.
entries.notes: Staffordshire Potteries. Subsequently Grimwades Ltd.

entries.name: Grimwades Ltd.
entries.works: Winton, Upper Hanley and Elgin Potteries, Stoke
entries.notes: Staffordshire Potteries. Formerly Grimwade Bros. Royal Winton is the best-known trade name.

entries.name: W. R. Midwinter (Ltd.)
entries.notes: Staffordshire Potteries. Early wares were generally unmarked. Pre-war marks 2664–5, post-war marks 2666–72. Group letter explained on Godden's page 295.

entries.name: Susie Cooper China Ltd.
entries.notes: Staffordshire Potteries. Subsequently "Susie Cooper Ltd.", same mark used.

entries.name: Susie Cooper Pottery (Ltd.)
entries.notes: Staffordshire Potteries. Miss Cooper (Mrs. C. F. Barker) was formerly employed decorating wares for A. E. Gray & Co., c. 1925–30. Renamed "Susie Cooper Ltd." c. 1961.

entries.name: Royal arms with ROYAL IRONSTONE CHINA JOHNSON BROS ENGLAND
entries.looks_like: The royal arms with lion and unicorn; ROYAL IRONSTONE CHINA in an arc above, JOHNSON BROS and ENGLAND below.
entries.means: Made by Johnson Bros. (Hanley) Ltd. (Hanley Pottery (and other Hanley Potteries), Hanley (and at Tunstall, c. 1899–1913)). Distinguishing name "Johnson Bros." found on several impressed or printed marks of differing design: name of the individual pattern is often included, 1883–1913. Godden's heading mark for the firm; many differing designs carry the name Johnson Bros. and often a pattern name.
entries.single_source: Godden (1964) only so far; Cushion & Honey (1956), Kovel (1986) and the firms' own histories not yet matched mark by mark.
entries.reads: ROYAL IRONSTONE CHINA / [royal arms] / JOHNSON BROS / ENGLAND

entries.name: ALFRED MEAKIN
entries.looks_like: The words ALFRED MEAKIN, impressed or printed on the base.
entries.means: Made by Alfred Meakin (Ltd.) (Royal Albert, Victoria and Highgate Potteries, Tunstall). Distinguishing details of several impressed or printed marks of differing design, 1875–. Note the addition of "Ltd." after 1897. Shared description with 2582: the name Alfred Meakin on marks of differing design; Ltd. added after 1897.

entries.looks_like: A globe, ruled with meridians, crossed by a ribbon lettered ALFRED MEAKIN.

entries.name: B
entries.looks_like: A single swash capital B with a long curl.
entries.means: Made by Booths (Limited) (Church Bank Pottery (and Swan and Soho Potteries from c. 1912), Tunstall). Painted or printed mark on reproductions of antique Worcester porcelains. The Worcester square seal mark (no. 4315) also occurs. It should be noted that these Booth reproductions are in opaque earthenware, not porcelain as are the originals. Variations of this mark occur, 1905+. WARNING: used on Booth reproductions of antique Worcester, in opaque earthenware, not porcelain; the Worcester square seal also occurs. Do not read as Worcester.

entries.means: Made by Josiah Spode (Stoke-on-Trent). Printed mark in black on stone-china, c. 1805-15. Printed in blue, c. 1815-30. The bottom half also occurs alone. entries.name: SPODE ICH DIEN
entries.looks_like: The words SPODE / ICH DIEN, printed on the base.
entries.means: Made by Josiah Spode (Stoke-on-Trent). A very rare printed mark on a porcelain plate with blue border and rose painted centre has been reported. It comprises the Prince of Wales' feather crest with the word "Spode" below and the motto "Ich Dien"; this may be a special mark for a Royal service, c. 1806-10. Messrs. Spodes were appointed Potters to the Prince of Wales in 1806. Very rare; Prince of Wales' feathers over SPODE and ICH DIEN. N.B. Many modern COPELAND marks include the name SPODE.

entries.name: AAO (or other letters impressed in sets of three)
entries.looks_like: The words AAO (or other letters impressed in sets of three), impressed on the base.
entries.means: Made by Josiah Wedgwood (& Sons Ltd.) (Burslem, c. 1759+; Etruria, c. 1769+; Barlaston, 1940-). Impressed three-letter date marks on earthenwares from 1860 onwards, see Table. It should be noted that the first letter which should denote the month was sometimes misplaced and is the second letter. Three impressed letters: month letter, potter's mark, year letter (the third letter is the year). Godden's table pages 658-659: third letter O=1860 ... Z=1871, A=1872 ... N=1885, O=1886 ... Z=1897, A=1898 ... I=1906 (letters repeat); from 1907 a '3' replaces the first letter, from 1924 a '4'; after 1930 month number then last two figures of year (1A 32 = January 1932). Month letters differ 1860-4 and 1864-1907 (see book). Standard impressed WEDGWOOD also occurs with the three letters. From 1891 ENGLAND should occur.

entries.means: Made by Ralph Wedgwood (& Co.) (Burslem, c. 1785-96; Ferrybridge Pottery, Yorkshire, c. 1796-1801 (see page 246)). Good quality creamwares of the 1790-1800 period occur with this impressed mark. Probably made by Ralph Wedgwood & Co. at the Hill Works, Burslem, before 1796, or by Tomlinson, Foster, Wedgwood & Co. of the Ferrybridge Pottery after Ralph Wedgwood joined them; this use ceased about 1801. Not the Tunstall firm Wedgwood & Co. (Ltd.). Also see Ferrybridge Pottery.

entries.means: Made by Minton (various titles) (Stoke). Painted mark on early porcelains, c. 1800–30. The mark occurs with or without pattern numbers under. entries.name: FELSPAR CHINA N° M
entries.looks_like: A floral scroll cartouche with FELSPAR CHINA curved round a pattern number and M.
entries.means: Made by Minton (various titles) (Stoke). Very many printed marks occur with the initials of the various partnerships M = c. 1822–36, M & B = c. 1836–41, M & Co. = 1841–73, M & H = 1845–68. Other examples have the name in full. entries.name: Crown with CLEWS WARRANTED STAFFORDSHIRE
entries.looks_like: A crown inside a circle, with CLEWS across the top, WARRANTED down the right and STAFFORDSHIRE round the left and bottom.
entries.means: Made by James & Ralph Clews (Cobridge Works, Cobridge). Impressed mark often found on good quality blue printed earthenwares. The wording reads: "Clews, Warranted Staffordshire". See companion illustrated encyclopaedia. Many printed marks also occur and these incorporate the name "Clews", c. 1818–34, see note below. On bill-heads these potters are described as "Potters to Her Imperial Majesty, the Empress of all the Russians". N.B. Reproductions have been made of Clews blue printed earthenwares; these have a faked mark similar to mark no. 919. The faked marks are very clearly stamped, not blurred as are most of the marks on original specimens. Reproductions of Clews blue printed earthenwares carry a faked mark like this one; the fakes are very clearly stamped, not blurred as on most originals. Many printed marks also incorporate the name Clews, c. 1818–34. Godden adds that the china wares of c. 1821–5 do not seem to be marked.

entries.name: Society of Arts gold medal legend with Rose & Co. Coalport Salop

entries.means: Made by Coalport Porcelain Works (John Rose & Co.) (Coalport, Shropshire (at Stoke-on-Trent from c. 1926)). The printed marks reproduced below were used for a few years from June 1820. Several slight variations were used, the first two are very rarely seen. It is probable that version number 948, with the addition of the word “improved”, was used slightly later than mark number 947. Nos. 945-8 left to right; the first two very rare; 948 adds the word improved; marks reproduced from specimens, not clean cuts. Wording within the circles is hard to read.

entries.means: Made by Coalport Porcelain Works (John Rose & Co.) (Coalport, Shropshire (at Stoke-on-Trent from c. 1926)). The printed marks reproduced below were used for a few years from June 1820. Several slight variations were used, the first two are very rarely seen. It is probable that version number 948, with the addition of the word “improved”, was used slightly later than mark number 947. Nos. 945-8 left to right; the first two very rare; 948 adds the word improved; marks reproduced from specimens, not clean cuts. Wording within the circles is hard to read.

entries.means: Made by Coalport Porcelain Works (John Rose & Co.) (Coalport, Shropshire (at Stoke-on-Trent from c. 1926)). This anchor mark with a “C” above occurs painted in blue on a Coalport copy of a Chelsea porcelain vase in the Victoria and Albert Museum. ... Other Coalport copies of Chelsea have a gold anchor, larger in size than that found on the originals, c. 1845–55. Copies Chelsea's anchor mark; the larger gold anchor on Coalport copies of Chelsea is a warning against mistaking them for originals.

entries.name: A Susie Cooper PRODUCTION. CROWN WORKS, BURSLEM, ENGLAND
entries.looks_like: A leaping antelope or gazelle above a small oval, with A Susie Cooper PRODUCTION. CROWN WORKS, BURSLEM, ENGLAND lettered below.
entries.means: Made by Susie Cooper Pottery (Ltd.) (Crown Works, Burslem). Printed marks, also signature alone, c. 1930– . The name "Crown Works" does not occur before 1932. "Crown Works" in the mark means 1932 or later. First of 1048–9.
